source_statement: Investigate an intermediate hexatic phase for 2D Riesz gases, having rapid positional decorrelation and slow six-fold orientational decorrelation. The source discusses s>2, and jellium s=0,1, without a single fixed quantified statement.
working_precisification: Classical short-range s>2, positive activity, a nonempty beta interval, stationary isotropic DLR states, truncated density two-point decay bounded by C(1+r)^(-q) with q>2, and two-sided bond covariance decay c(1+r)^(-eta) to C(1+r)^(-eta) with 0<eta<2 for an explicitly specified six-fold bond field. This stronger precisification is ours; exponential positional decay is not required.

status_search.result: No verified phase-existence proof recovered; bounded search does not establish present openness.

prior_attempt.result: Global-angle mixture: zero one-point sixth harmonic does not imply vanishing two-point orientational order.

scar.lesson: A successful local calculation or green pipeline is not proof of the hardest unchecked piece.
